subject: On-site preflight: compute segmentation & volume-binding decisions
messages:
From: Samuel Ortiz <sam.ortiz@springboard.ai>
To: hiro.tanaka@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com
Cc: itops@springboard.ai, procure@springboard.ai
Date: Fri, 05 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Springboard on-site preflight: compute segmentation & volume-binding

Hi Hiro / Marissa,

Thanks again for scheduling the on-site intake for our private cluster next month. Before the field team arrives we want to lock the high-level deployment choices so the datacenter crew can pre-stage racks and switch configs. Two items surfaced in our ops review that need Redwood direction:

1) Compute segmentation - Springboard prefers a separated class for model-serving (GPU), model-build (CPU heavy), and infra/agents (small CPU + egress). They asked whether Redwood expects dedicated node pools per workload or if taints/affinities on shared pools are acceptable.

2) Volume binding / PV strategy - we currently run NetApp iSCSI blockstore in the room. CSI driver version the storage team will install supports VolumeBinding WaitForFirstConsumer but they want to confirm whether we rely on dynamic binding or if static LVM pre-provisioning is required for models >1TB.

Attached: a short preflight checklist and our physical network diagram. Can you confirm Redwood's recommended defaults and any host-level kernel or MTU settings the site should preconfigure? Also cc'ing Procurement so they can track any hardware requests.

--
Samuel Ortiz
Head of Ops, Springboard AI
sam.ortiz@springboard.ai
From: hiro.tanaka@redwood.com
To: sam.ortiz@springboard.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.com
Cc: itops@springboard.ai
Date: Fri, 05 Jun 2026 10:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Springboard on-site preflight: compute segmentation & volume-binding

Samuel — thanks for the clear note and the attachments. High-level guidance below; I'll work with Marissa to capture the operator-run checklist we want onsite.

Brief answers up-front:
- Compute segmentation: we recommend dedicated node pools for GPU (model-serving & inference) and a separate CPU-heavy pool for batch model-build/training orchestration. Infra/agents should be on a small, tainted pool to protect control-plane latency. Dedicated pools make capacity planning + autoscaling simpler and reduce noisy-neighbor risk for latency-sensitive inference.

- Volume binding: prefer dynamic provisioning with the storage team's CSI driver using VolumeBinding=WaitForFirstConsumer for PVs that are latency-sensitive (models, WALs). For very large model images (>1TB) we recommend static provisioning of pre-formatted block devices (LUKS-encrypted LVM) as a fallback — this reduces attach latency at scale and gives you predictable placement when the blockstore backend has provisioning constraints.

Site configuration notes (actionable):
- MTU: 9000 (jumbo) across compute, ToR, and SAN switch fabric where possible; validate end-to-end.
- Dual ToR + MLAG/BGP: dual-homed ToR with MLAG is fine; if using BGP for pod egress announce we need L2 adjacency for the storage fabric.
- Kubelet: --eviction-hard=memory.available<200Mi,nodefs.available<10% and --protect-kernel-defaults=true; set kubelet --serialize-image-pulls for faster startup.
- Kernel settings: disable THP for model containers (transparent_hugepage=never); ensure iommu=on if using device assignment.

Marissa — can you confirm whether Redwood will provide a static PV provisioner playbook for the LUKS/LVM path and a CSI compatibility matrix? I can capture the site-level prep items into the shared checklist once we agree.

Thanks,
Hiro Tanaka
Director, Deployment Engineering
Redwood Inference
hiro.tanaka@redwood.com
From: marissa.cole@redwood.com
To: sam.ortiz@springboard.ai, hiro.tanaka@redwood.com
Cc: neha.kapoor@redwood.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 05 Jun 2026 15:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Springboard on-site preflight: compute segmentation & volume-binding

On Fri, Jun 5, 2026 at 10:04 AM hiro.tanaka@redwood.com wrote:
> Samuel — thanks for the clear note and the attachments. High-level guidance below; I'll work with Marissa to capture the operator-run checklist we want onsite.

Adding the checklist items and specifics from infra/ops side:

Preflight decision table (short):
- Node pools:
  * gpu-inference (taint: nimbus=gpuserve:NoSchedule) — r5-class with 1-2 GPUs/node, 2 local NVMe per node for KV cache (ephemeral).
  * cpu-build (no GPU, higher vCPU) — used for batch builds and conversion pipelines.
  * infra (tainted) — control-plane proxies, logging, node-exporter, sidecars; smaller instances, anti-affinity across ToR.

- Storage classes:
  * fast-block-scs (dynamic, WaitForFirstConsumer, io-profile=low-latency) -> CSI NetApp iSCSI
  * large-model-static -> static LUKS/LVM on pre-attached volumes (admin-created) for >1TB images
  * ephemeral-nvme -> local PV (storageclass: local-ephemeral, volumeBindingMode: Immediate) for model caches and scratch (do NOT use for critical state)

- Snapshots & backup: Ensure CSI snapshot CRDs are installed and E2E tested; snapshot schedule for model checkpoints daily.

Operator tasks to complete before arrival:
- Storage team to pre-create /dev/mapper structures for large-model-static volumes and hand off mapping to Redwood ops on day-0.
- Switch team to validate MTU 9000 across VLANs used by compute/storage and document per-rack QoS.
- Provide the SAN LUN attachment matrix so Redwood can pre-generate PV manifests for static volumes.

Neha — can you confirm CSI version support for NetApp + Kubernetes 1.26? Karthik — please review the ToR bonding notes below and confirm whether we should require BGP for pod egress or rely on SNAT from ToR.

Attachments referenced above include the compatibility matrix I exported.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Senior Site Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
From: hiro.tanaka@redwood.com
To: sam.ortiz@springboard.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.com, neha.kapoor@redwood.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.com
Cc: itops@springboard.ai
Date: Sat, 06 Jun 2026 16:38:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Springboard on-site preflight: compute segmentation & volume-binding — final decisions and day-0 runbook

Thanks everyone — summary and day-0 owner assignments below (please treat as the canonical plan for the site crew):

Decisions (final):
- Dedicated node pools for gpu-inference, cpu-build, infra (affirmed).
- Use dynamic provisioning with CSI NetApp driver + WaitForFirstConsumer for general workloads; require static LUKS/LVM provisioning for any model images >1TB (Procurement to allocate LUNs).
- Local NVMe allowed for ephemeral caches (local-ephemeral storageclass) but with node-affinity and short retention policies.
- MTU 9000 recommended end-to-end; fall back to 1500 only if SAN fabric does not support jumbo frames (site to test).

Day-0 runbook (owners):
- Springboard SAN team: pre-attach LUNs for large-model-static; provide LUN -> host mapping (due: 2026-06-20).
- Network team (Springboard): validate MTU & provide QoS per-rack (due: 2026-06-18).
- Redwood Ops (Marissa): bring static PV provisioning playbook & automated LUKS/LVM script; test PV manifest generation with provided mapping (due: 2026-06-22).
- Redwood Platform (Neha): confirm CSI 3.x compatibility with k8s 1.26 and provide a small patch list if needed (due: 2026-06-16).
- Deployment Engineering (Karthik): finalize ToR egress plan (BGP vs SNAT) and produce final network diagram for sign-off (due: 2026-06-17).

Open questions for Procurement: cost/schedule impact of pre-attached LUNs vs on-demand provisioning; Procurement please provide options by 2026-06-12.

I'll post the consolidated preflight checklist to the shared Drive and notify the field team once the items above are confirmed. If no objections, we'll treat this as the preflight scope for the June on-site.

Regards,
Hiro Tanaka
Director, Deployment Engineering
Redwood Inference
hiro.tanaka@redwood.com
